F1.quote: Drawing from a diverse range of perspectives, the Responsible Sourcing workstream aims to develop recommendations and actionable resources to improve the working conditions of these professionals.
F1.claim: the workstream defined by its operator: it aims to develop recommendations and actionable resources to improve the working conditions of data enrichment professionals
F1.lineage: what it is: recommendations and resources to improve data enrichment workers' conditions

F2.quote: Data labelers, data cleaners, and others who contribute human judgment to artificial intelligence (AI) systems play a critical role in developing this technology.
F2.claim: the workers it concerns: data labelers, data cleaners and others who contribute human judgment to AI systems, critical to developing it
F2.lineage: the labor: data enrichment work is essential to AI

F3.quote: Data enrichment is a broadly defined term that encapsulates various types of data preparation and cleaning as well as human-review processes.
F3.claim: data enrichment defined: data preparation and cleaning, and human-review processes

F4.locus: 'What Is Data Enrichment?' ¶2 s4 and list
F4.quote: Enriched data is essential for the training and validation of supervised learning models, the dominant form of applied AI. … Content moderation … Validating algorithmic outputs and models
F4.claim: enriched data is essential for training and validating supervised models; the human-review work includes content moderation and validating algorithmic outputs and models
F4.checked_against: saved text B1.txt (sha256 d47b580df5f9a987…), whitespace-normalised; multi-part quote joined by ' … ', each part checked

F5.quote: Despite being an essential component of AI development, data enrichment work has for too long been both out of sight and out of mind for AI developers. … This disconnect leads to a devaluing of data enrichment work, poor working conditions for data enrichment workers, and, often, worse outcomes for AI development itself.
F5.claim: the diagnosis: data enrichment work out of sight of AI developers, the disconnect devaluing the work, bringing poor working conditions and, often, worse outcomes for AI development
F5.lineage: the diagnosis: invisibility, devaluing and its costs
F5.checked_against: saved text B1.txt (sha256 d47b580df5f9a987…), whitespace-normalised; multi-part quote joined by ' … ', each part checked

F6.quote: From AI developers we’ve heard sentiments like “We feel we must care about the transparency of our supply chain. But there is no transparency in data labeling. Guidelines on how to navigate this would be very useful.”
F6.claim: AI developers quoted: no transparency in data labeling; guidelines would be useful
F6.lineage: the opacity of the data supply chain

F7.quote: The Responsible Sourcing workstream addresses these questions by working to provide actionable guidance for data scientists, AI engineers, and product managers, to empower these critical ecosystem players to do their part in ensuring healthy and fair working conditions across the data supply line.
F7.claim: whom it addresses: actionable guidance for data scientists, AI engineers and product managers, toward healthy and fair working conditions across the data supply line

F8.locus: breadcrumb; Updates list (first and last items)
F8.quote: Workstreams / AI, Labor, and the Economy Responsible Sourcing Across the Data Supply Line … Responsible AI Starts with the Data Supply Chain Michael George, Eliza McCullough Apr 29, 2026 … Developing Guidance for Responsible Data Enrichment Sourcing B Cavello Dec 22, 2020
F8.claim: a workstream of PAI's AI, Labor, and the Economy programme, its updates dated from 22 December 2020 to 29 April 2026
F8.lineage: the operator, the programme and the dates
F8.checked_against: saved text B1.txt (sha256 d47b580df5f9a987…), whitespace-normalised; multi-part quote joined by ' … ', each part checked

F9.quote: This white paper, “Responsible Sourcing of Data Enrichment Services,” addresses an often overlooked aspect of the development process and what AI practitioners can do to help improve it: the working conditions of data enrichment professionals, without whom the value being generated by AI would be impossible.
F9.claim: the white paper defined by its publisher: on the working conditions of data enrichment professionals and what AI practitioners can do to improve them
F9.lineage: the white paper: what AI practitioners can do

F10.quote: This paper’s recommendations will be an integral part of the shared prosperity targets being developed by Partnership on AI (PAI) as outlined in the AI and Shared Prosperity Initiative’s Agenda.
F10.claim: its recommendations to become part of PAI's shared prosperity targets
F10.lineage: the operator, the programme and the dates

F11.quote: this process is highly labor-intensive and often requires data enrichment workers to review, classify, and otherwise manage massive amounts of data. Despite the foundational role played by these data enrichment professionals, a growing body of research reveals the precarious working conditions these workers face. This may be the result of efforts to hide AI’s dependence on this large labor force when celebrating the efficiency gains of technology.
F11.claim: enrichment is labor-intensive; research reveals precarious conditions; this may result from efforts to hide AI's dependence on this labor force
F11.lineage: the diagnosis: invisibility, devaluing and its costs

F12.locus: 'Data Enrichment Choices Impact Worker Well-being' ¶1 s2
F12.quote: The decisions AI developers make while procuring enriched data have a meaningful impact on the working conditions of data enrichment professionals.
F12.claim: procurement decisions of AI developers shape the working conditions of data enrichment professionals

F13.locus: 'Data Enrichment Choices Impact Worker Well-being' ¶1 s4 and list
F13.quote: this paper covers worker-centric considerations for AI companies making decisions in: selecting data enrichment providers, running pilots, designing data enrichment tasks and writing instructions, assigning tasks, defining payment terms and pricing, establishing a communication cadence with workers, conducting quality assurance, and offboarding workers from a project.
F13.claim: the paper's scope: eight decision points, from selecting providers and pilots to payment terms, quality assurance and offboarding
F13.lineage: the white paper: what AI practitioners can do

F14.quote: This paper draws heavily on insights and input gathered during semi-structured interviews with members of the AI enrichment ecosystem conducted throughout 2020 as well as during a five-part workshop series held in the fall of 2020. The workshop series brought together more than 30 professionals from different areas of the data enrichment ecosystem
F14.claim: method: interviews through 2020 and a five-part workshop series in fall 2020 with more than 30 professionals of the ecosystem

F15.quote: Additional work is needed to ensure industry practices recognize, appreciate, and fairly compensate the workers conducting data enrichment.
F15.claim: stated limit: additional work is needed for industry practice to recognize and fairly compensate data enrichment workers
F15.lineage: the stated limits: a starting point; more work needed

F16.quote: Data enrichment workers, the people who label and annotate the training data on which these systems are built, are essential to AI, yet their contributions are frequently overlooked. Research has shown that these workers often face low wages, unclear expectations, and inadequate support. The AI data supply chain remains largely opaque and unregulated, leaving these workers without sufficient protections.
F16.claim: data enrichment workers label and annotate training data, essential and overlooked; research shows low wages, unclear expectations, inadequate support; the AI data supply chain opaque and unregulated
F16.lineage: the opacity of the data supply chain

F17.quote: The conditions under which data is produced directly affect the quality, safety, and reliability of the AI that is built on it.
F17.claim: the conditions of data production affect the quality, safety and reliability of the AI built on it
F17.lineage: conditions and the quality of AI

F18.quote: Since 2020, Partnership on AI has spotlighted the importance of raising standards across the data enrichment supply chain to advance positive outcomes for the people powering these systems. In 2023, PAI released a first-of-its-kind AI job impact assessment and recommendations for the field with its Guidelines for AI and Shared Prosperity, which included recommendations around the responsible sourcing of data.
F18.claim: since 2020 PAI has worked to raise standards across the supply chain; its 2023 Guidelines for AI and Shared Prosperity included responsible-sourcing recommendations
F18.lineage: the operator, the programme and the dates

F19.quote: But raising standards also requires practical tools that companies can put to use. As part of our work to support the implementation of the Guidelines, finalized versions of two of our resources, developed and refined in conversation with companies throughout the supply chain, as well as worker advocates, are now available: the Vendor Engagement Guidance, which helps companies have more accountable conversations with their downstream vendors about worker treatment, and the Transparency Template, which outlines what companies should be monitoring and publicly reporting about their data enrichment practices.
F19.claim: finalized versions (April 2026) of the Vendor Engagement Guidance (accountable conversations with downstream vendors about worker treatment) and the Transparency Template (what companies should monitor and publicly report about their data enrichment practices)
F19.lineage: the vendor guidance and transparency template (2024–2026)

F20.quote: PAI’s work in raising standards for data enrichment workers continues on through our support of our long-standing partner Business for Social Responsibility (BSR) via their initiative focused on labor rights in the AI data supply chain.
F20.claim: the work continues through PAI's support of BSR's initiative on labor rights in the AI data supply chain

F21.quote: Legislative efforts are also underway that are focused on increasing the pay received by data enrichment workers and increasing transparency in the data enrichment supply chain, with more to come. Responsible AI cannot be achieved without the responsible treatment of the people whose labor makes AI possible.
F21.claim: legislative efforts on data enrichment workers' pay and supply-chain transparency are underway; responsible AI requires the responsible treatment of the people whose labor makes it possible
F21.lineage: the labor: data enrichment work is essential to AI

F22.quote: While these datasets can only be prepared by humans, the data enrichment workers who do so (performing tasks like data annotation, data cleaning, and human review of algorithmic outputs) are an often-overlooked part of the development lifecycle, frequently working in poor conditions continents away from AI-developing companies and their customers.
F22.claim: data enrichment workers, often overlooked, frequently working in poor conditions continents away from AI developers
F22.lineage: who supplies the labor: faraway workers under precarious conditions

F23.quote: we recognize the variety of employment statuses that can exist in the data enrichment industry, including independent contractors on self-service crowdsourcing platforms, subcontractors of data enrichment providers, and full-time employees.
F23.claim: 'workers' covers independent contractors on crowdsourcing platforms, subcontractors of providers and full-time employees

F24.quote: This case study documents an effort to put that paper’s recommendations into practice at one AI developer: DeepMind, a PAI Partner.
F24.claim: the case study documents putting the white paper's recommendations into practice at one AI developer, DeepMind, a PAI Partner

F25.quote: This case study serves as one such resource, offering a detailed account of DeepMind’s process and learnings for other organizations interested in improving their data enrichment sourcing practices.
F25.claim: the case study as a resource: DeepMind's process and learnings for other organizations

F26.quote: said that these new processes felt efficient and helped them think more deeply about the impact of their work on data enrichment workers
F26.claim: DeepMind's researchers reported the new processes efficient and prompting thought about the impact on workers

F27.locus: case study executive summary ¶10 s2; table of contents
F27.quote: Furthermore, to identify where the implemented changes fall short of ideal, we plan to continue developing this work through engagement and convenings. … Limitations of Case Study Applicability
F27.claim: stated limit: the implemented changes may fall short of ideal; the case study carries a section on the limits of its applicability
F27.lineage: the stated limits: a starting point; more work needed
F27.checked_against: saved text B4.txt (sha256 0bb8a51aadb30e75…), whitespace-normalised; multi-part quote joined by ' … ', each part checked

F28.quote: Their latest white paper Responsible Sourcing of Data Enrichment Services examines the working conditions of data enrichment professionals, and seeks to: Critically evaluate the impact of the industry’s current practices on workers; Explore practices the industry can adopt to improve worker well-being; and Advance the discourse around the future of data enrichment work and the indispensable role it plays in AI development.
F28.claim: Sama on the white paper: it evaluates the impact of current practices on workers, explores practices to improve well-being, and advances the discourse
F28.lineage: the white paper: what AI practitioners can do

F29.quote: Despite their foundational role, working conditions for data enrichment professions can be precarious: they can face wage uncertainty, low pay and limited career growth opportunities.
F29.claim: Sama: working conditions can be precarious: wage uncertainty, low pay, limited career growth

F30.quote: Since data labeling is a key part of this equation, it was important for Sama to partner with PAI: to both share our lessons learned from several years of striving for more ethical supply chains, and to continue to learn from industry peers about responsible AI.In fall of 2020, Sama participated in the five-week series of Responsible Sourcingworkshops held by PAI
F30.claim: Sama, a data labeling vendor, partnered with PAI, sharing its lessons 'striving for more ethical supply chains', and took part in the five-week workshop series of fall 2020
F30.note: B2 says 'a five-part workshop series'; B5 says 'the five-week series': distinct instances (§3.6), carried as stated. 'Responsible Sourcingworkshops' is the page's text.

F31.quote: While more work and research is needed, Responsible Sourcing of Data Enrichment Services shares actionable insight that practitioners can use as a starting point to raise important conversations with internal stakeholders.
F31.claim: Sama: more work and research is needed; the paper is a starting point for conversations
F31.lineage: the stated limits: a starting point; more work needed

F32.quote: Despite growing awareness of their often precarious working conditions, there has been limited transparency about how AI practitioners are sourcing enriched data from these workers and little guidance on how they should. To help fill this gap, Partnership on AI (PAI) shared the Responsible Data Enrichment Sourcing Library, a set of resources AI organisations can use to formalise their data enrichment practices and have a positive impact on the lives of data enrichment workers.
F32.claim: the library, entered in the OECD.AI catalogue: resources AI organisations can use to formalise their data enrichment practices, filling a gap of transparency and guidance
F32.lineage: what it is: recommendations and resources to improve data enrichment workers' conditions

F33.quote: Local Living Wages Spreadsheet Template: A Google Sheets template to create a centralised resource for looking up living wage information for each of the geographic areas an organisation sources data enrichment labour from.
F33.claim: the library's resources include a living-wages spreadsheet template for each area an organisation sources data enrichment labour from

F34.quote: Our primary objective in sharing these resources is to lower the barriers for companies interested in improving their data enrichment sourcing practices. Our intention is for the library to serve as a resource for champions within companies to advocate for their organisations to adopt responsible data enrichment sourcing practices.
F34.claim: objective: lower the barriers for companies; the library a resource for champions within companies

F35.quote: Maturity: Implemented in multiple projects … Usage rights: Open source/Permissive
F35.claim: the catalogue entry classifies the tool as implemented in multiple projects, with open source/permissive usage rights
F35.note: The catalogue's form as filled; the field's own pages name one implementation (B4, B8) and state no licence (B1, B8 footer: '© 2026 Partnership on AI | All Rights Reserved').

F36.quote: Disclaimer: The tools and metrics featured herein are solely those of the originating authors and are not vetted or endorsed by the OECD or its member countries.
F36.claim: the catalogue's limit: entries are the originating authors' own, not vetted or endorsed by the OECD

F37.locus: 'AI is powered by data enrichment workers…' s1–2
F37.quote: To create today’s machine learning (ML) models, AI developers require enriched datasets, vast quantities of information organized by humans so that it can be understood by machines. While these datasets can contain millions of individual entries, the extensive labor that goes into building them is often overlooked, performed by faraway workers under precarious conditions.
F37.claim: enriched datasets are organized by humans; the extensive labor is often overlooked, performed by faraway workers under precarious conditions
F37.lineage: who supplies the labor: faraway workers under precarious conditions

F38.locus: '…but their contributions are often overlooked' s1–2
F38.quote: Research shows these workers often face inconsistent and inappropriate compensation for their work, unclear instructions, lack of recognition, and emotional and physical stress related to long, ad-hoc working hours. Under-appreciating the importance of this work doesn’t just impact the wellbeing of these workers, it also affects the quality of the data AI technology is built on.
F38.claim: research shows inconsistent and inappropriate compensation, unclear instructions, lack of recognition and stress from long ad-hoc hours; under-appreciation also affects data quality

F39.locus: 'How can AI companies make data enrichment work better?' s1–2
F39.quote: AI companies and the people that work for them have the power to improve the lives of data enrichment workers. When designing a project involving enriched data, there are five, worker-centric guidelines that AI practitioners should follow.
F39.claim: five worker-centric guidelines that AI practitioners should follow when designing a project involving enriched data

F40.quote: 1. Ensure all data enrichment workers are paid above the local living wage … AI Practitioners must pay workers/participants at least the living wage for their location. … including time spent reading instructions, going through any training and reviewing work before submission.
F40.claim: guideline 1: pay all data enrichment workers above the local living wage, counting time spent reading instructions, training and reviewing work before submission
F40.lineage: guideline 1: the living wage, counting the time around the task
F40.checked_against: saved text B8.txt (sha256 389441dd67f7afef…), whitespace-normalised; multi-part quote joined by ' … ', each part checked

F41.quote: The per task rate should be based on the hourly living wage, divided by the adjusted number of tasks that can be completed in an hour. … We would discourage using a simple median, as this could cause half the workers to receive an insufficient wage.
F41.claim: the per-task rate from the hourly living wage; against a simple median, which could leave half the workers with an insufficient wage
F41.lineage: guideline 1: the living wage, counting the time around the task
F41.checked_against: saved text B8.txt (sha256 389441dd67f7afef…), whitespace-normalised; multi-part quote joined by ' … ', each part checked

F42.quote: AI Practitioners should pay for any work completed by workers to compensate for their time, being mindful that mass rejections of work completed without opportunities for redress impact the workers’ livelihood. The only exceptions should be in the cases of obvious abuse or fraud.
F42.claim: pay for any completed work; mass rejections without redress harm livelihoods; exceptions only for obvious abuse or fraud
F42.lineage: payment for completed work and contestable rejections

F43.quote: 2. Design and run a pilot before launching a data enrichment project … 3. Identify appropriate data enrichment workers for the desired task
F43.claim: guidelines 2 and 3: run a pilot before launching; identify appropriate workers for the task
F43.checked_against: saved text B8.txt (sha256 389441dd67f7afef…), whitespace-normalised; multi-part quote joined by ' … ', each part checked

F44.quote: 4. Provide verified instructions and/or training materials for data enrichment workers … Note: As discussed in Guideline 1, time spent reading instructions or in training should be compensated. … 5. Establish clear and regular communication mechanisms … including contesting any rejected work.
F44.claim: guidelines 4 and 5: verified instructions and training, the time compensated; clear communication, including contesting rejected work
F44.lineage: payment for completed work and contestable rejections
F44.checked_against: saved text B8.txt (sha256 389441dd67f7afef…), whitespace-normalised; multi-part quote joined by ' … ', each part checked

F45.quote: These guidelines, based on PAI’s Responsible Sourcing of Data Enrichment Services white paper and developed in partnership with DeepMind, have been tested and adopted by DeepMind organization-wide.
F45.claim: the guidelines, based on the white paper and developed with DeepMind, tested and adopted by DeepMind organization-wide

F46.locus: 'What resources can help practitioners meet these guidelines?'
F46.quote: Data Enrichment Vendor Comparison Template A Google Sheets template for comparing various vendors of data enrichment services and surfacing relevant worker-centric considerations … DeepMind Case Study A case study detailing why DeepMind committed to the Data Enrichment Sourcing Guidelines, how they did it, and the impact of adopting these recommendations
F46.claim: the library's resources include the vendor comparison template and the DeepMind case study (six resources)

F47.quote: To ensure our guidance truly improves conditions for data enrichment workers, we welcome feedback: … If you are interested in acting on these guidelines and resources or have feedback on how they can be improved, please get in touch.
F47.claim: stated limit: feedback invited from practitioners, workers and the AI community, to ensure the guidance improves conditions
F47.lineage: the stated limits: a starting point; more work needed

F48.quote: Partnership on Artificial Intelligence to Benefit People and Society, otherwise known as Partnership on AI (PAI), is a nonprofit coalition committed to the responsible use of artificial intelligence.
F48.claim: the operator: PAI, a nonprofit coalition committed to the responsible use of AI
F48.lineage: the operator, the programme and the dates

F49.quote: The Partnership on AI was publicly announced on September 28, 2016, with founding members Amazon, Facebook, Google, DeepMind, Microsoft, and IBM
F49.claim: PAI announced 28 September 2016, DeepMind among its founding members

F50.claim: the AI, Labor, and the Economy program: a platform uniting economists, worker representative organizations and partners
